messages.author: 558f30f3e1ce07a3
messages.subject: Starting Values when Hessian is Singular Error Occurs
parts:
Hello everyone,

I'm very new to occupancy modeling and found good examples for unmarked. I found a bit of code online which worked pretty well in transitioning my data to a umf and get the null model. However, any additional variables I add, I receive the Hessian is Singular Error. I can't seem to figure out the correct starting values to advance my models. I'm working on a simple one season, one species occupancy model across an elevational gradient; it's a part of a much larger data set but I just wanted to work on a small part of the data before tackling the larger set. I tried to look through some past posts on the subject but can't figure it out. Any help/advice would be greatly appreciated. Here's my code and the file with my data.

options(download.file.method="libcurl")
library(unmarked)
library(reshape)
library(rjags)
library(R2WinBUGS)
library(R2OpenBUGS)
setwd("C:\\Users\\lougd15\\Documents\\Research\\Analysis\\Occup")
occak <- read.csv("Akodon_Test.csv", header=TRUE)
head(occak)
summary(occak)
n <- dim(occak)
head(n)
y <- occak[,2:69]#Days
head(y)
siteCovs <- occak[, c("site","seeds","elev", "slope", "hill", 
                        "aspect", "habitat")]#Site Covariates
head(siteCovs)
##Observation Covariates
obsCovs<-list(date=occak[,c("date.1", "date.2", "date.3","date.4", "date.5", 
                            "date.6", "date.7", "date.8", "date.9",
                            "date.10", "date.11", "date.12", "date.13", 
                            "date.14", "date.15", "date.16", "date.17", 
                            "date.18", "date.19", "date.20", "date.21",
                            "date.22", "date.23", "date.24", "date.25", 
                            "date.26", "date.27", "date.28", "date.29", 
                            "date.30","date.31", "date.32", "date.33", 
                            "date.34", "date.35", "date.36", "date.37", 
                            "date.38", "date.39", "date.40", "date.41", 
                            "date.42", "date.43", "date.44", "date.45", 
                            "date.46", "date.47", "date.48", "date.49", 
                            "date.50", "date.51", "date.52", "date.53", 
                            "date.54", "date.55", "date.56", "date.57", 
                            "date.58", "date.59", "date.60", "date.61", 
                            "date.62", "date.63", "date.64", "date.65", 
                            "date.66", "date.67", "date.68")])
head(obsCovs)
summary(obsCovs)
occak <- unmarkedFrameOccu(y = y, siteCovs = siteCovs, 
                           obsCovs = obsCovs)##Officially an unmarked frame
summary(occak)
# Standardize covariates to improve estimation by using the scale function
# (default "centers" the data by subtracting the mean from each individual data 
# point, then "scales" the data by dividing each point by the standard deviation
# of all points)
obsCovs(occak) <- scale(obsCovs(occak))
summary(occak)
# Model fitting. "fm1" returns data on the logit scale. You must use the function
# backTransform to get data on the probability scale. 
(fm1 <- occu(~1 ~1, occak))
backTransform(fm1, type="state")
backTransform(fm1, type="det")
##Building the Models
fm2 <- occu(~1~elev, occak, starts=c(-0.1, -1.2, 0))

Best,
Danny

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: AW: [unmarked] Starting Values when Hessian is Singular Error Occurs
parts:
Hi Danny,

 

Have you tried to scale your site covariates ?

 

Also note that with so many occasions, and with per-occasion p of about 0.2, the combined P is essentially equal to 1, so if you’re interested in factors that affect occurrence rather than detection, you can simply run logistic regressions of the observed presence-absence status at a site, i.e., model obsz <- apply(y, 1, max)

 

Best regards  -- Marc

Just a emphasize Marc's comment:  Standardizing the site covariates fixes the issue and you can just use the default starting values:

siteCovs(occak) <- scale(siteCovs(occak))
fm2 <- occu(~1~elev, occak)

Jim
